chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارُ عَنْ ظَرِيفِ بْنِ نَاصِحٍ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ع قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me; Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Zarif ibn Nasih, who raised it to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), saying:

chunks.arabic_text: إِنَّمَا شِيعَةُ عَلِيٍّ ع الْمُتَبَاذِلُونَ فِي وَلاَيَتِنَا الْمُتَحَابُّونَ فِي مَوَدَّتِنَا الْمُتَزَاوِرُونَ لِإِحْيَاءِ أَمْرِنَا إِنْ غَضِبُوا لَمْ يَظْلِمُوا وَإِنْ رَضُوا لَ مُسْرِفُوا بَرَكَةٌ لِمَنْ جَاوَرُوا وَسِلْمٌ لِمَنْ خَالَطُوا

translations.en: The Shia of Ali (peace be upon him) are those who exchange favors in our leadership, love each other for our affection, and visit one another to revive our affair. When they are angry, they do not oppress; and when they are pleased, they do not exaggerate. They are a blessing for their neighbors and peace for their companions.

en.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a foundational definition of 'Shi'a' not merely as a political faction but as a community bound by 'Mawadda' (affection) and active social engagement, specifically through 'Tazawur' (visiting one another) to revive their cause. The description of emotional equilibrium—avoiding oppression in anger and excess in joy—reflects the Shia ideal of balanced character, while the promise of being a source of blessing for neighbors connects directly to the Prophetic tradition of social responsibility.
en.seo_question: What are the defining moral and social characteristics of the Shia according to this hadith?

key_terms.شِيعَةُ عَلِيٍّ: Shia of Ali (followers/disciples of Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْمُتَبَاذِلُونَ: Those who exchange favors/gifts with one another
